tagline: Leading global infrastructure operator providing trading, clearing, and settlement services for capital markets
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI reflects the organic growth of Deutsche Börse's diversified business model, excluding non-recurring items from treasury results.
company_description: Deutsche Börse AG operates as an international exchange organization in Germany, rest of Europe, the United States, and the Asia-Pacific. The company operates through four segments: Investment Management Solutions; Trading & Clearing; Fund Services; and Securities Services. Its Investment Management Solutions segment offers financial data, analytics, and software-as-a-service solutions including research, data collection, data analysis, and the provision of indices, analytics and investment management software to institutional investors, banks, and corporate clients. The Trading & Clearing segment engages in the development and operation of markets and trading systems for securities, derivatives, commodities, currencies, digital assets, and other asset classes. This segment handles settlement of transactions through clearing houses. Its Fund Services segment provides infrastructure and services for fund processing, including order routing, settlement, custody, data and distribution support for investment funds. kpis.name: Net Revenue Growth (ex-Treasury)
kpis.explanation: Year-over-year growth in net revenues from core business operations excluding treasury result fluctuations
kpis.description: Net revenues without treasury result increased 12% year-over-year to EUR 1,434 million in Q1 2026 (Q1 2025: EUR 1,277 million), driven by continued structural growth across Fund Services, Securities Services, and software solutions.
kpis.signal: Strong structural growth despite geopolitical volatility and macroeconomic headwinds in Q1 2026

kpis.name: Total Net Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total net revenues including treasury result from banking and similar business operations
kpis.description: Total net revenues including treasury result grew 9% to EUR 1,638 million in Q1 2026 (Q1 2025: EUR 1,507 million). Treasury result declined to EUR 204 million from EUR 230 million due to lower interest rate environment and reduced cash deposits.
kpis.signal: Treasury headwinds moderating; overall revenue growth demonstrates business resilience amid market volatility

kpis.name: EBITDA without Treasury Result
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, excluding treasury result, reflecting core operational profitability
kpis.description: EBITDA without treasury result increased 18% to EUR 803 million in Q1 2026 (Q1 2025: EUR 682 million), demonstrating significant scalability advantages in the core business despite inflation and investment effects.
kpis.signal: Strong operating leverage and scalability of diversified business model demonstrated by above-revenue growth rate

kpis.name: EBITDA with Treasury Result
kpis.explanation: Total EBITDA including treasury result from banking operations, representing record profitability
kpis.description: Total EBITDA including treasury result reached record EUR 1,007 million in Q1 2026 (Q1 2025: EUR 912 million), representing 10% year-over-year growth.
kpis.signal: Record EBITDA level achieved despite moderating treasury contributions, reflecting operational excellence

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Profit attributable to Deutsche Börse AG shareholders after all expenses and taxes
kpis.description: Net income attributable to Deutsche Börse AG shareholders increased 11% to EUR 585 million in Q1 2026 (Q1 2025: EUR 525 million), driven by higher operating profits partially offset by increased tax expense.
kpis.signal: Strong bottom-line growth reflecting operating performance and capital efficiency

kpis.name: Earnings Per Share
kpis.explanation: Net income per share calculated on actual share count
kpis.description: Diluted earnings per share increased 12% to EUR 3.21 in Q1 2026 (Q1 2025: EUR 2.86), benefiting from both higher net income and share count reduction from the EUR 500 million buyback program launched in February 2026.
kpis.signal: Per-share earnings growth outpacing net income growth due to share buyback program reducing share count

kpis.name: Cash EPS
kpis.explanation: Earnings per share before purchase price allocation effects from acquisitions, showing cash generation
kpis.description: Cash EPS (before purchase price allocation effects) reached EUR 3.40 in Q1 2026 (Q1 2025: EUR 3.05), representing 11% growth and reflecting true cash-based earnings power.
kpis.signal: Adjusted EPS demonstrates strong underlying cash generation and operational performance

kpis.name: Operating Costs
kpis.explanation: Combined personnel and operating expenses excluding volume-dependent costs
kpis.description: Operating costs increased 4% to EUR 626 million in Q1 2026 (Q1 2025: EUR 601 million), driven by inflation, investments, and integration costs, while benefiting from FX headwinds. Cost growth significantly trails revenue growth of 12%, validating scalability model.
kpis.signal: Cost discipline maintained with growth (4%) well below revenue growth (12%), demonstrating operating leverage

kpis.name: DPS
kpis.explanation: Total amount paid in dividends per share over the fiscal year.

kpis.name: Cap Return
kpis.explanation: Annual total: dividends paid + share buybacks.
kpis.description: Dividends + cumulative buybacks (2022-2026) in EUR billions.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Portion of net income redistributed. >80% = potentially unsustainable.

kpis.name: EPS
kpis.explanation: Net income divided by the weighted average number of diluted shares over the fiscal year. Measures the company's ability to generate earnings per share: basis for Payout Ratio (DPS / EPS).
kpis.description: 5-year history (2021-2025). Source: yfinance income statement (Diluted EPS).

risks.title: Increased regulation as a financial holding
risks.summary: BaFin is reviewing a potential classification of Deutsche Börse AG as a financial holding, which could impact its capital requirements and capital structure, despite its current status not being subject to this framework.
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in the Risikofaktoren section, the risk is expressed with concerned language ("könnte sich u. a. auf unsere Eigenmittelausstattung auswirken"). The trend is stable, but the risk is central due to its link to the group's fundamental regulatory classification. The Regulation category is highly strategic for a market operator.

risks.title: Dependence on CSDR and EMIR regulations
risks.summary: Clearing activities of Clearstream, Eurex and European Commodity Clearing strictly depend on compliance with CSDR and EMIR regulations, non-compliance of which could jeopardize their license and operational functioning.
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly cites CSDR requirements for Clearstream and EMIR for Eurex, with strong language ("ausschlaggebend", "zu jeder Zeit eingehalten"). The risk is stable but critical, as these regulations structure all clearing activities. The Regulation category is central.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and operational continuity
risks.summary: As an operator of critical infrastructure, Deutsche Börse is exposed to cyberattacks or system failures that could disrupt markets, with major systemic and regulatory consequences.
risks.score_rationale: Although the word "cyber" is not explicitly cited, the text mentions anomaly detection, operational losses, and systemic risks related to critical systems. The language is preventive but urgent. The risk is stable and major, as financial market continuity depends on technological resilience.

risks.title: Operational risks in clearing houses
risks.summary: Activities of Clearstream and clearing houses (Eurex, ECC) are exposed to systemic errors, technological failures, or human errors that could impact financial stability and counterparty confidence.
risks.score_rationale: The text describes the use of simulation models and operational risk measures for regulated entities. The language is technical and serious. The risk is stable, but critical due to its link to central clearing and settlement processes.

risks.title: Competition on trading platforms
risks.summary: Deutsche Börse faces increasing competition from alternative trading platforms (MTF, dark pools) and international players, threatening its market share in equities, derivatives, and post-trading services.
risks.score_rationale: The risk is not explicitly named, but the strategic context of an exchange operator implies intense competition. The relative silence in the text suggests constant vigilance. The risk is stable, but structural for the business model.

risks.title: Dependence on critical technology providers
risks.summary: Deutsche Börse's technology infrastructure relies on specialized vendors for data management, cybersecurity, and trading systems, whose failure could disrupt operations.
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions automation, IT systems, and dependence on specific software (e.g., ESG reporting). The language is factual but implies vulnerability. The risk is stable, with high weight due to system interdependence.

risks.title: ESG data governance risks
risks.summary: The collection, verification, and publication of ESG data (emissions, energy) are subject to risks of errors or inconsistencies, potentially harming reputation and leading to penalties under new European standards.
risks.score_rationale: The text describes processes for sustainability reporting (ESRS, ESG), with controls in place. The language is proactive but reveals exposure. The risk is rising, as ESG regulatory requirements are rapidly increasing.
